raised.claim: Adding any enumerated beer ID bypasses the prohibition on a whole-class where clause.
raised.why_it_breaks: A proposal with beer_ids: [1] and where: [{col: 'review_class', op: '=', value: 'matcher_bug'}] passes legality. Because rowSatisfiesScope treats the cohort and where as alternatives, every future matcher_bug row also matches, including IDs outside the cohort. The issue can therefore declare exactly the whole-class scope this guard is meant to reject.

raised.claim: Verdicts attached to newly proposed issues are never checked against those issues' scopes.
raised.why_it_breaks: A zero-candidate row can reference a new issue scoped to candidates_count > 0 with an empty beer_ids list. The scope is legal, so the key is allowed and the verdict is published and persisted despite contradicting the scope. The same attachment would be rejected if the issue already existed.

raised.claim: The saturation guard does not include attachments already accepted in the current plan.
raised.why_it_breaks: With postCreationRows equal to 11 and 50 matching verdicts targeting the same issue, every verdict sees 11 and passes. The resulting comment adds all 50 rows, taking the issue to 61 rather than stopping at 12. Neither the supplied count nor a separate planned-attachment count is incremented.

raised.quote:
const body = `${issue.body}\n\n${renderScopeBlock(issue.scope)}`;
        const number = await github.createIssue({ title: issue.title, body, labels: issue.labels });
raised.claim: A triage-scope block in the model-authored issue body overrides the supposedly authoritative rendered scope.
raised.why_it_breaks: The model can supply a body containing a valid triage-scope block before the structured scope appended here. On the next run, parseScopeBlock selects the first block, so it reads the model-authored scope instead of issue.scope. A broad class-only block can silently replace a narrow validated scope; a malformed first block instead makes the issue unscoped.

raised.claim: Guard counters are omitted whenever the model returns a verdict for every input row, even if the guards reject every verdict.
raised.why_it_breaks: covered counts IDs in analysis.verdicts before planning, not accepted verdicts. If all 50 input rows receive verdicts targeting an unscoped or saturated issue, covered remains 50 and this log never runs, although all rows are skipped and will return tomorrow. Absence downgrades are similarly invisible when coverage is complete.

raised.claim: One empty probe permits an absence verdict even when the other probe returned the actual beer.
raised.why_it_breaks: For a brewery-alias mismatch, a brewery-only probe can return an empty string while the name-only probe returns the exact beer under its canonical brewery. The OR expression still marks absence as proved and preserves not_on_untappd, which blocks the paid fallback despite affirmative evidence that the beer exists.

raised.claim: Newly downgraded absence verdicts are reported as wontfix in the daily outcome.
raised.why_it_breaks: A not_on_untappd verdict without probe evidence now enters plan.quiet as matcher_bug. The job's quiet-result loop increments notOnUntappd only for not_on_untappd and increments wontfix for every other class. Consequently, a batch of ten recoverable matcher_bug downgrades is announced as ten wontfix rows even though the database contains no such classifications.

raised.claim: Post-creation counting compares timestamp strings without normalizing GitHub and database timestamp precision.
raised.why_it_breaks: GitHub supplies created_at values such as 2026-08-14T06:00:00Z, while the job writes reviewed_at using toISOString(), such as 2026-08-14T06:00:00.500Z. SQLite compares these TEXT values lexically, making the later fractional-second review sort before the creation timestamp. Legitimate post-creation rows within that second are omitted from the saturation count.

raised.quote: ALTER TABLE enrich_failures ADD COLUMN issue_number INTEGER;
raised.claim: The new authoritative issue link is not invalidated when a failure is reopened for triage.
raised.why_it_breaks: After a row is attached to an issue, recordEnrichFailure clears review_class, review_note, and reviewed_at when candidates_count crosses the zero/nonzero boundary, but leaves the new issue_number intact. The resulting untriaged row still claims an authoritative association with its previous issue even though its review and evidence have been invalidated; rejected future verdicts can leave that stale association indefinitely.

raised.quote:
export const V23_BACKFILL_SQL = `
  UPDATE enrich_failures
     SET issue_number = CAST(substr(review_note, instr(review_note, '→ #') + 3) AS INTEGER)
   WHERE review_note LIKE '%→ #%'
     AND CAST(substr(review_note, instr(review_note, '→ #') + 3) AS INTEGER) > 0;
raised.claim: The backfill reads the first arrow reference rather than the authoritative appended issue suffix.
raised.why_it_breaks: A legacy note such as 'previous routing → #347; corrected → #405' is assigned issue_number 347 because instr finds the first occurrence. Arbitrary review prose can contain an earlier reference, while the job appends its actual issue reference at the end. Such rows are migrated to the wrong issue and distort saturation counts.

raised.claim: The strict tool schema accepts scope terms that the runtime schema rejects, allowing one malformed proposal to fail the entire batch.
raised.why_it_breaks: A term such as {col: 'candidates_count', op: '>', value: '0'} satisfies this tool schema but fails ScopeTermSchema, which requires a numeric value. Unknown columns or operators also satisfy the tool schema. AnalysisSchema then rejects the entire response rather than letting the planner drop only the invalid proposal, losing otherwise usable verdicts.

raised.claim: Appending the scope after unrestricted prose can hide all routing constraints from the next run's model.
raised.why_it_breaks: If issue.body is at least 2,000 characters, buildTriagePrompt's existing body slice excludes the entire newly appended scope. The planner still reads the full body and enforces those unseen constraints. A model can repeatedly select the issue based on its visible prose while every proposed attachment violates the hidden scope and returns untriaged the next day.

raised.claim: The saturation count forgets historical attachments when failure records are cleared or reopened.
raised.why_it_breaks: An issue with 12 post-creation attachments stops accepting rows, but clearEnrichFailure deletes those records when beers match, and a zero/nonzero candidate transition nulls reviewed_at. Either operation reduces this count without removing the existing GitHub examples, allowing further batches onto an issue that has already reached the stated attachment limit. If the intended threshold is cumulative post-creation attachments rather than currently reviewed failures, this does not enforce it.
